artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $N$ be a closed hyperbolic surface, i.e., a closed orientable Riemannian 2-manifold of constant curvature $-1$. By an embedded billiard table in $N$ we mean a compact, embedded, simply connected smooth domain $\Omega \subset N$ with smooth boundary $\partial\Omega$. A closed billiard trajectory in $\Omega$ is a piecewise geodesic curve in $\Omega$ whose interior segments are geodesic arcs in $N$ and which reflects elastically (angle of incidence equals angle of reflection) at each boundary impact, returning to its starting point and direction after finitely many reflections. Denote by $\Omega\text{-sys}$ the infimum of the lengths of all closed billiard trajectories in $\Omega$ (the billiard systole).

Question: Does there exist a sequence $\{\Omega_i\}_{i\in\mathbb{N}}$ of embedded simply connected billiard tables in $N$ such that 
$$\Omega_i\text{-sys} \longrightarrow \infty \quad \text{as } i \to \infty?$$
artifact.status_search_result: No published resolution was found. The question is posed as an open problem in the context of quantitative symplectic geometry and billiards, and a positive answer would reportedly yield novel examples in the field. Available literature on systoles of hyperbolic surfaces and on billiards in hyperbolic settings does not appear to settle this specific question.

status_evidence.title: Finiteness in Polygonal Billiards on Hyperbolic Plane
status_evidence.snippet: Studies billiards on the hyperbolic plane but does not address embedded simply connected billiard tables in closed hyperbolic surfaces with billiard systole tending to infinity.
status_evidence.claim: Related work on hyperbolic billiards does not resolve the question.

status_evidence.title: Graphs of Large Girth and Surfaces of Large Systole
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs hyperbolic surfaces with large systole, but for closed surfaces of growing genus, not for embedded simply connected billiard subdomains of a fixed closed hyperbolic surface.
status_evidence.claim: Standard systole constructions do not yield the requested billiard table sequence.
